audit.action: cite a better source for the same coding
audit.reasoning: Coding 'fixed-dominant', rule initial (10 100 1000...) rests on Southwell 1992 OPD p.3, quote confirmed verbatim in the copy fetched sources now. The fuller primary source, Southwell & Southwell 1972 'Phonemes and Orthography of Komba' sec. 5.3 (fetched sources now, read from the scan), says 'Stress is predictable. The primary stress occurs on word initial syllables and secondary stress on following alternate syllables', with marked examples of 2-7 syllables all showing initial primary and secondaries on syllables 3, 5, 7 (final odd secondary optional). This confirms fixed initial primary stress and refines the record with a secondary-stress rule and word-length range; no weight sensitivity, no lexical exceptions, no tone mentioned. If anything the 1972 statement ('predictable', no exceptions) would support strict fixed-initial rather than merely dominant, but no recode of the primary-stress class is n

sources.quote: Stress is predictable. The primary stress occurs on word initial syllables and secondary stress on following alternate syllables.
